doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Health insurance and union coverage
summary: Coverage only while working in theater.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Right. What did you do for things like retirement and health insurance and all those things all those years?

When you’re working in the theater you’re covered for health insurance. I never used it. Now I’ve got to pay. It’s over four hundred dollars for my wife and I each, per quarter. I don’t even want to get into that.

And then you go to a doctor, like my wife has been going to a doctor, and they say, “oh yeah, you’re covered.” And then all of a sudden you start getting bills. And you call and say how come I’m paying all that money and where is it going? But then when you’re doing the theater, in other words, when you’re working you’re covered. When you don’t work you’re not covered. It’s kind of backwards. No?
Well the union is backwards. But that’s the way it is.
